evidence: M-O s.v. Anglican: lītūrgia Anglicāna, id est certus modus ōrātiōnis (Tursellinus, 1652)
terms.comment: The Eucharistic service of the Orthodox churches and of the Eastern Catholics; in the Byzantine rite, the Liturgies of St John Chrysostom and St Basil. In the Latin rite the same service is the Mass (missa). Lītūrgia is the Greek λειτουργία, a public service; in Neo-Latin it also means a church’s whole order of worship (Morgan–Owens).
Greek σύναξις, a gathering (Lewis & Short); sacra synaxis, the Eucharistic assembly (Morgan–Owens).

liturgia.against: not in Lewis & Short; Neo-Latin texts write it without marks
liturgia.html: Greek λειτουργία: ει and ου are long, and Latin writes them ī and ū, as in Nīlus (Νεῖλος) and Mūsa (Μοῦσα).

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. Anglican; service: mass.
Lītūrgia is not in Lewis & Short, Traupman or Levi–Bini.
